name.x-prompt: What is the name of the package? (eg: @example/package-name)

description.x-prompt: What is the description of the package?

x-prompt.message: What is the platform of the package?

items.label: Node.js only
items.description: For packages that run in Node.js (CLIs, Nx executors/generators, server utilities). Can use Node APIs like fs, path, and process. Not intended to be bundled into a browser app.

items.label: Browser only
items.description: For packages meant to run in the browser (React components, UI utilities, client-side helpers). Should avoid Node-only APIs. Typically built as ESM and consumed by bundlers like Vite/Webpack.

items.label: Node.js and Browser
items.description: For packages that work in both environments. Best for "universal" utilities (e.g., parsing, formatting, shared types/helpers). Must avoid environment-specific APIs or provide separate builds/exports for Node vs browser.

dropLocation.description: The location to drop the package
dropLocation.x-prompt: Where do you want to drop the package? (leave blank for default)

baseTsconfigPath.description: The path to the base tsconfig.json
baseTsconfigPath.x-prompt: Where is the base tsconfig.json? (leave blank for default)

addProjectFile.description: Whether to add a project file
addProjectFile.x-prompt: Do you want to add a project file? (leave blank for default)

tsupOptionsFile.description: Path to a JSON file containing tsup configuration options. The file should conform to the tsup-options.schema.json schema.
